articles.title: Rajpal Yadav tells Supreme Court his next film will be on his 16-year cheque-bounce battle, reveals the title 'Solah Sawan Jhel Ke'
articles.summary: Rajpal Yadav personally addressed the Supreme Court on Wednesday during the hearing of his cheque-bounce case.
articles.body: Rajpal Yadav personally addressed the Supreme Court on Wednesday during the hearing of his cheque-bounce case. He spoke about the money and career he says he has lost over the last 13 years, including a Rs 17 crore loss on his 2012 film 'Ata Pata Laapata'. The court also accepted his proposal to sell his ancestral property to clear the dues.Rajpal Yadav speaks directly to the Chief JusticeThe hearing took a lighter turn when the Chief Justice encouraged Rajpal Yadav to return to filmmaking. According to the Bar and Bench report, CJI Surya Kant told him, "Koi nayi movie aa rahi hai? Koi achi si movie banake logo ko dobara entertain karo. Aapki image dobara ban jaegi. Humare yahan kuch advocate bhi ache actor hain, unko leke koi movie banao (Is there a new movie coming out? Make a good movie and entertain people again; that will help rebuild your image. We have some lawyers here who are also good actors. Can make a movie featuring them)."Rajpal Yadav replied that he had already thought of a title for a film based on his experiences between 2010 and 2026."Sir, 2010 se 2026 tak jo hua, uska title bhi humne socha hai, Solah Sawan Jhel Ke (Sir, I have even thought of a title for everything that happened from 2010 to 2026: Solah Sawan Jhel Ke)," he said.The title roughly means "having endured 16 monsoons". It drew attention because it points to the long legal and financial troubles he described in court.The actor has been part of the cheque-bounce dispute for several years, and the matter has continued in court since the early 2010s. Wednesday's exchange offered a rare light moment in an otherwise serious hearing.Supreme Court accepts plan to sell ancestral propertyThe Supreme Court accepted Rajpal Yadav's proposal to sell his ancestral property to clear the dues linked to the case. The bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana, also noted that he had made arrangements to pay Rs 2 crore immediately through demand drafts.Yadav submitted demand drafts worth Rs 1.15 crore. The remaining Rs 85 lakh is to be paid by a prospective buyer of his property by October 12. articles.title: Quote of the day by Gene Hackman: 'I had only small goals. To go from $48 a week off-Broadway to $90 a week as a supernumerary on Broadway seemed like stealing,' a powerful life lesson on humility and patience
articles.summary: Explore Gene Hackman's philosophy of achieving success through small goals and humility, as he reflects on his journey from earning $48 a week to becoming an Oscar-winning actor.
articles.body: Gene Hackman never wanted to be a movie star. He wanted a paycheck. He wanted to work. He wanted to act, and if acting paid the rent, that was enough. A man who would later win Academy Awards for 'The French Connection' and 'Unforgiven' was once thrilled by the idea of doubling his weekly pay from $48 to $ 90. For a man with simple goals, Hackman sure has built one of the most celebrated careers in American film historyIn a 1974 interview with The Guardian, he looked back on his early days in New York. He said he only had little goals, and seeing things take a beautiful turn seemed too good to be true.Today’s quote of the day by Gene Hackman reads: "I had only small goals. To go from $48 a week off-Broadway to $90 a week as a supernumerary on Broadway seemed like stealing"What does the quote by Gene Hackman really mean?It means to follow your goals one step at a time. Instead of rushing to complete it all in one go, completing small goals one at a time makes the bigger goals not feel like a burden anymore. Hackman explains that at that time, his only focus was to just get a promotion; Hackman wasn't being modest. He genuinely didn't think he was special. He was voted "least likely to succeed" at the Pasadena Playhouse alongside his classmate Dustin Hoffman. He was told he wouldn't amount to anything. He flunked out of acting school. He spent years working odd jobs, doing summer stock, and taking bit parts. So when he finally got to Broadway, even as a supernumerary, essentially a bit player or extra, it felt like a miracle.He says it almost apologetically. He was supposed to go from off-Broadway to a supernumerary role. Instead, he skipped straight into a supporting part. Hackman frames it as if he got lucky, as if he skipped a rung on the ladder and didn't deserve it. He's not saying life was easier. He's saying it was clearer. The goals were small. The wins were tangible. Doubling your pay is a real thing. You can hold it in your hand. It's harder to feel the weight of an Oscar after a while. But $90 a week when you were making $48. That's something you remember forever.How is the quote by Gene Hackman still relevant today?People are obsessed with big wins, and they skip over the small steps because they don't feel like steps at all. They feel like standing still. But Hackman's quote says the opposite. The small goals are the ones that keep you moving.His words also speak to anyone who feels like they're behind. Hackman didn't become a leading man until his late thirties. He won his first Oscar at 42. He was broke. He was told he wouldn't make it. He kept going anyway. Not because he had a grand vision. Because he had small goals.Hackman also never let Hollywood change how he saw himself. "I was trained to be an actor, not a star," he told Larry King in an interview. "I never had the aspirations to be a star. I wanted to be an actor. A movie actor, a theater actor, that's all I ever wanted to do". That's the same philosophy. The work matters. Not the accolades.Early life of Gene HackmanEugene Allen Hackman was born on January 30, 1930, in San Bernardino, California, to Eugene Ezra Hackman and Anna Lyda Gray. His father operated a newspaper printing press. The family moved around a lot, eventually settling in Danville, Illinois. His childhood wasn't easy. His father left when Hackman was 13. The memory stayed with him for the rest of his life. Hackman recalled years later. He grew up in a broken home, often in trouble, often fighting with authority figures.He left home at 16. He lied about his age to join the Marine Corps. He spent four and a half years in the service, serving in Japan and China. He was not a model soldier. "I have trouble with direction, because I just have always had trouble with authority," he told Larry King. "I was not a good Marine. I made corporal once and was promptly busted."After being discharged, he studied journalism at the University of Illinois on the G.I. Bill. He dropped out. He worked a string of menial jobs. He moved to New York at 22 to try to become an actor. He was over 30 when he finally enrolled at the Pasadena Playhouse. He flunked out after three months. He got one of the lowest grades the school had ever given.Gene Hackman's rise to fameIn 1964, he was cast in the Broadway play 'Any Wednesday'. That led to a small role in 'Lilith', starring Warren Beatty. Beatty remembered him. When Beatty was casting 'Bonnie and Clyde' in 1967, he cast Hackman as Buck Barrow. That role earned him his first Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor.He was nominated again for 'I Never Sang for My Father' in 1970. Then came 'The French Connection' in 1971. He played Jimmy "Popeye" Doyle, the tough, New York detective. He won the Oscar for Best Actor. He was 42. He won his second Oscar for 'Unforgiven' in 1992. He played Sheriff "Little Bill" Daggett, a sadistic lawman in Clint Eastwood's revisionist Western. He was 62. He had been working steadily for thirty years. He had done comedy, drama, villainy, and everything in between. He was one of the most versatile actors of his generation.He retired from acting in 2004 after 'Welcome to Mooseport'. He moved to Santa Fe, New Mexico, with his wife, Betsy Arakawa. He wrote novels. He painted. He lived a quiet life away from Hollywood. He died on February 18, 2025, at the age of 95. He left a philosophy in his wake. Small goals. Small wins. Keep going. And never stop being amazed by how it all turns out.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Power Rangers x Ninja Kidz brings back Jason, Kimberly, Trini, Billy and Zack with a surprising new mythology and Mighty Morphin fans may love it
articles.summary: It is a strange time to be a Power Rangers fan.
articles.body: It is a strange time to be a Power Rangers fan. The franchise’s long-awaited live-action reboot for Disney+ has been shelved, while Power Rangers Cosmic Fury, the most recent television season, concluded in 2023. In the middle of that long gap, Power Rangers x Ninja Kidz, a free-to-watch YouTube series, has quietly emerged as the closest thing fans have to a new live-action Power Rangers show in 2026.And surprisingly, it is not just a glorified toy commercial.An official Power Rangers series built around toysPower Rangers x Ninja Kidz is not a conventional television season, but it is officially licensed and was produced in partnership with Playmates, Hasbro’s partner for the latest Power Rangers toy line. The series supports the Re-Ignition range of action figures and merchandise, with episodes available to watch for free on YouTube.Considering its origins as part of a merchandise push, the series could easily have felt like an extended advertisement. Instead, it makes a genuine attempt to tell a new Power Rangers story, bringing the Ninja Kidz cast into the world of Mighty Morphin Power Rangers and building a mythology of its own.Why it feels like Mighty Morphin Power RangersThe appeal of the original Mighty Morphin Power Rangers was never just about colourful suits and giant robots. The series combined martial arts, superhero-style action, larger-than-life villains, comedy and a sense of adventure that made its deliberately campy world so much fun.Power Rangers x Ninja Kidz understands that formula.The recast versions of Jason, Kimberly, Trini, Billy and Zack retain the spirit of the original team, while the Ninja Kidz performers bring an energetic, action-heavy style that fits naturally into Ranger battles.Visually, the series also knows exactly what longtime fans want. The Ranger suits retain the instantly recognisable colours, helmets and dinosaur-inspired designs of the original era, while additional armour details give them a more contemporary appearance.The villains receive a similar treatment. Rita Repulsa, Lord Zedd and Goldar return with updated designs, but the changes are restrained enough to preserve their familiar identities rather than turning them into completely different characters.A new story hiding inside familiar Power Rangers mythologyWhere the series becomes more interesting is in the way it reworks established mythology.Instead of simply recreating the original Mighty Morphin Power Rangers storyline, Power Rangers x Ninja Kidz takes some major liberties. In this version of the story, Lord Zedd wins, forcing some of the Rangers to escape to Rafkon. There, they encounter a younger version of Zayto, the Red Ranger from Power Rangers Dino Fury.Meanwhile, Tommy Oliver takes a very different path. Rather than becoming the Green Ranger fans know from the original series, he operates as a mysterious lone hero known as the Dragon, fighting against Zedd’s rule.Even Bulk gets a surprising reinvention, moving beyond his familiar comic-relief role to become a more capable ally.These changes give the series something important: a reason to exist beyond nostalgia.The Power Rangers franchise is in an unusual live-action droughtThe series arrives at a particularly uncertain moment for the franchise.Disney+ reportedly spent around a year and a half developing a new live-action Power Rangers series with Jonathan E. Steinberg and Dan Shotz, known for Percy Jackson and the Olympians, before the project was shelved. With no replacement live-action television series announced, Power Rangers x Ninja Kidz currently occupies an unusual position in the franchise’s 2026 landscape.It is obviously not a replacement for a full-scale television revival. Its YouTube format, short runtime and toy-line origins put limits on what it can accomplish.But that does not make it disposable.The series carries storylines across episodes, expands on established mythology and pulls characters and ideas from different generations of Power Rangers. Most importantly, it appears to understand why the original series worked in the first place.For fans who have been waiting for the franchise to return to live-action, Power Rangers x Ninja Kidz may not be the revival they were promised. But during an unusually quiet period for the Rangers, it is a surprisingly entertaining stopgap and one that deserves more credit than its toy-commercial origins might suggest.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2010, Paul Walker travelled to Haiti after the devastating earthquake; how the experience inspired the disaster-relief organisation he founded
articles.summary: Long before Paul Walker became remembered not only as the star of the Fast & Furious franchise but also for his humanitarian work, the actor had been
articles.body: Long before Paul Walker became remembered not only as the star of the Fast & Furious franchise but also for his humanitarian work, the actor had been looking for ways to help people affected by natural disasters. That instinct turned into something much bigger after the devastating earthquake that struck Haiti in January 2010.On January 12, 2010, a magnitude 7.0 earthquake hit Haiti, with the epicentre near the capital, Port-au-Prince. In the days that followed, Walker gathered a group of friends and first responders and travelled to Haiti with medical supplies and other essentials. According to Reach Out WorldWide (ROWW), the organisation he later founded, the trip became the first unofficial deployment of what would become the disaster-relief group.Walker did not want to help from a distanceWalker had already spoken about wanting to be directly involved when disasters struck. In a 2010 Men’s Health interview, he described himself as a “do-er” and recalled his desire to help after disasters including the tsunami in Sri Lanka and the earthquake in Indonesia. He said he wanted to be able to gather people with useful skills and go where they were needed.The Haiti earthquake gave him the opportunity to act on that idea. Walker and his friends put together a team and supplies before travelling to the disaster zone. Contemporary accounts say the group brought items including medical equipment and water-filtration supplies.The team reached Haiti five days after the earthquake. They were dropped by helicopter at an orphanage roughly 20 miles outside Port-au-Prince and immediately began assisting with patient treatment and transportation, transporting supplies and establishing shelters and tents.The experience changed the way Walker viewed disaster reliefWhat Walker encountered in Haiti was more than the destruction shown in news reports. He and the team saw first-hand how difficult it could be to get appropriately skilled people and resources into the areas where they were most urgently required.Following the Haiti response, Walker founded Reach Out WorldWide. The organisation was built around a simple idea: quickly bring people with specialised skills to communities affected by natural disasters and work alongside existing local resources.Walker also remained personally involved. He funded deployments, travelled with teams and participated in relief work himself. Later in 2010, he travelled to Chile following the earthquake and tsunami there, where his organisation delivered water and medical aid. In 2011, he joined relief efforts in Alabama after devastating tornadoes, helping clear damaged homes and debris.A different legacy from his Hollywood careerFor Walker, the work was not simply about attaching his name to a charitable cause. People who worked with him repeatedly described him as someone who wanted to be physically present and contribute.His friend Jesse Brisendine, who was part of the early Haiti effort, later recalled seeing Haitian families who had lost their homes yet were grateful for whatever they had managed to salvage. He remembered Walker watching as people gathered together, describing the moment as one in which Walker could see the impact of what the group had set out to do.Walker died in November 2013 at the age of 40, but the organisation that grew out of that 2010 Haiti mission continued his disaster-relief work. ROWW remains focused on deploying medical and disaster-relief professionals to communities affected by natural disasters.The Haiti earthquake therefore became a defining turning point in Walker’s life away from Hollywood. What began as a spontaneous decision to gather friends, supplies and skilled responders for a disaster thousands of miles away ultimately became the foundation of an organisation built around the very thing Walker believed in: showing up when people needed help most.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: The countdown to Superstar Rajinikanth’s 'Jailer 2' is getting sharper, as the film now enters the final phase before its theatrical release.
articles.body: The countdown to Superstar Rajinikanth’s 'Jailer 2' is getting sharper, as the film now enters the final phase before its theatrical release. Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, the action entertainer is set to hit screens worldwide on October 15 and has already created strong anticipation with its trailer, star-studded cast, and Anirudh Ravichander’s music. The sequel brings back the world of Muthuvel Pandian on a much bigger scale.'Jailer 2' gets UA 16+ certificate with 165-minute runtimeAs per the official announcement, 'Jailer 2' has completed its censor process and received a UA 16+ certification from the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC). The film’s certified runtime is said to be 165 minutes and 18 seconds, keeping it just under three hours. The makers are yet to make an official announcement regarding the certification and runtime. articles.body: Holly Madison has no problem with reality TV drama — as long as everyone is in on the joke. The "Girls Next Door" alum told Fox News Digital she would "100%" embrace manufactured conflict on a show like "Real Housewives of Las Vegas," but claimed manipulation by the "puppet masters" behind her former series contributed to lasting rifts among the cast. For years, Madison had seemingly closed the door on reality television, previously saying she would never return after her experience on "The Girls Next Door." But with time and a different perspective on how manufactured drama could work, she admitted she has reconsidered that hard-line stance. "You know what, I've changed my thought on that," the Grant a Gift Gala ambassador explained. "I would do manufactured drama if I was in on the joke. I always say that to Bridgette watching 'Girls Next Door,' I'm like, if we knew what the drama was and the three of us were gonna play it out on screen and not take it home with us, so to speak, when the cameras are done rolling, that would have been so much more fun to me than being manipulated from the puppet masters above." I would actually do manufactured drama, 100%. I would throw down on like a 'Real Housewives of Las Vegas.' I just don't want to be puppeted again." The former reality star also pointed to another major difference between the television landscape then and now: the audience. "Editing's crazy," she noted. "But I also appreciate that viewers are a little more sophisticated now. I mean, back in the 'Girls Next Door' days, they could edit something to be not what it was. Like anytime it's brought up or mentioned, it's kind of laughed about," Madison added. "So I'm glad that whoever's bringing it to their attention or bringing it up — because it's not me or their dad — whoever's bringing it up is bringing it up like it's a positive or a cool thing or a funny thing. articles.summary: Abhishek Pathak's crime thriller 'Drishyam 3' has crossed Rs 340 crore at the worldwide box office, and actor Ajay Devgn says its different storyline from
articles.body: Abhishek Pathak's crime thriller 'Drishyam 3' has crossed Rs 340 crore at the worldwide box office, and actor Ajay Devgn says its different storyline from the Malayalam film was not a rebellion. The Hindi version, which released after Jeetu Joseph's Malayalam film earlier this year, followed its own route, and Ajay Devgn feels it was a natural chain of events.Is 'Drishyam 4' on the cards?The Malayalam version, starring Mohanlal, did not get the strong response the franchise is known for, and Jeethu Joseph seems to be working on a fourth part. Although 'Drishyam 3' was billed as 'The Conclusion', Ajay Devgn hinted that the makers, like his clever character Vijay Salgaonkar, may have a trick up their sleeve."At the moment, it is a conclusion," Ajay Devgn told Gulf News, before adding, "I can't predict it." When pressed, he did not rule out another film. "The decision was, this is the conclusion. The decision right now is that this is the conclusion… Right now," he added.Hindi and Malayalam teams shared their scriptsAfter Abhishek Pathak and his father, Kumar Mangat Pathak, Panorama Studios acquired the franchise from the Malayalam makers, the two teams began working together. During the interview, Ajay Devgn revealed, "Honestly speaking, they had not decided to make a third one. We were toying with the idea, and I think all the writers worked out some ideas, and they didn't work. And finally, things fell into place."He added, "We spoke to them, and we were like, 'Let's make it; we have a script.' And then they said that they're also working on something, and they had a script. So we thought, 'Let's hear each of her out and decide what to do.'"The Hindi writers Abhishek Pathak, Aamii Keeyan Khan and Parveez Shaikh then exchanged scripts with Joseph, the writer of the Malayalam film.Why the Hindi team stuck to its own scriptAjay Devgn added, "Finally we came to the conclusion that this is a fabulous script, but it is most suited for their audience. And we were very confident about our script. So, then we decided that we will go ahead," recalled Devgn. "When you work hard and then you get something which is to the point, then you're confident enough to make it the way you want to make it."More about 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion'The cast also includes Tabu, Rajat Kapoor, Shriya Saran, Ishita Dutta, Jaideep Ahlawat, Prakash Raj and Kamlesh Sawant. articles.title: Michael Douglas rompe su silencio sobre una supuesta adicción al sexo: "No sé si me acosté con tantas mujeres"
articles.standfirst: El actor ha desmontado este mito durante la promoción de su autobiografía
articles.summary: El actor ha desmontado este mito durante la promoción de su autobiografía
articles.body: A sus 82 años, el actor estadounidense Michael Douglas ha roto su silencio sobre los históricos rumores de los años 90 sobre su supuesta adicción al sexo. Con motivo de la promoción de su primera autobiografía, titulada ‘One Helluva Ride’, el doble ganador del Oscar abordó el tema en una entrevista concedida al periódico británico The Times. El actor calificó la historia como una invención de los medios de comunicación y bromeó con la persistencia del mito: "No sé si me acosté con tantas mujeres. Yo no lo veo así. No, yo no. Yo era un producto sano de los años 60", ha afirmado, destacando que le parecía "curioso" que "los británicos estuvieran tan obsesionados con los temas sexuales". En concreto, Douglas atribuyó el origen del rumor a la prensa británica: "A un editor de un tabloide británico se le ocurrió esta historia, de la que, muchas gracias, aquí estamos hablando a mis 82 años". Con esto, desmiente de forma categórica que su ingreso en una clínica de rehabilitación en 1992 se debiera a una adicción sexual. A pesar de negar la adicción, el protagonista de ‘Instinto básico’ comparte detalles llamativos sobre su vida sentimental en el libro. Por ejemplo, habla de sus inicios con Catherine Zeta-Jones, confesando que cuando empezó a verse con su actual esposa, salía simultáneamente con otras cinco mujeres en ciudades distintas. Sin embargo, al formalizar su relación, Catherine Zeta-Jones le exigió exclusividad. "Ella me dijo que, si íbamos a seguir con esto, quería que fuera una relación monógama. Así que esa misma noche llamé a algunas mujeres con las que estaba saliendo, y ahí se acabó", relata el intérprete. Finalmente, en sus memorias también desvela facetas desconocidas de su pasado amoroso, incluyendo una relación sentimental con la actriz Kathleen Turner, quien fue su compañera de reparto en la icónica película ‘Tras el corazón verde’.

articles.title: Brad Pitt’s rise to fame: From Oklahoma’s suburbs to $400 million net worth; here’s all you need to know about the ‘F1’ star
articles.summary: Discover the rise of Brad Pitt from his humble beginnings in Oklahoma to becoming one of Hollywood's most celebrated actors, with insights into his personal life, major roles, and accomplishments including his $400 million net worth.
articles.body: Brad Pitt is one of Hollywood’s most iconic actors and influential producers, evolving from a heartthrob in the 1990s into a critically acclaimed Academy Award winner. Pitt has come a long way in his career, starting from almost nothing to now having a net worth of USD 400 million. Here is a look into his early life, his entry into the Hollywood industry, and how he became one of the most beloved stars in the industry.Brad Pitt’s early life and entry into the industryBrad Pitt was born as William Bradley Pitt on December 18, 1963, in Shawnee, Oklahoma, though he was raised in Springfield, Missouri. From a young age, Pitt grew up in a conservative Southern Baptist household and attended the University of Missouri, majoring in journalism with a focus on advertising. He had been interested in acting from a young age; however, he still went to college for a degree.However, just two weeks before he would have completed his degree in 1986, Pitt dropped out and drove all the way to Los Angeles to pursue acting seriously. In his early years in LA, to make ends meet, he often worked odd jobs, which included things like driving limousines, moving refrigerators, and dressing as a giant chicken for El Pollo Loco.Brad Pitt’s entry into Hollywood and his breakthrough roleThe actor made his acting debut in May 1987 when he scored a two-episode role on the soap opera ‘Another World,' while his feature film debut as a lead in the 1989 slasher movie ‘Cutting Class.’ His breakthrough came years later in 1991, when he played the role of the drifter J.D. in Ridley Scott's ‘Thelma & Louise.’ Following the release of this film, the star started booking major projects left and right.Some of his other critically acclaimed roles include ‘A River Runs Through It’ (1992), ‘Interview with the Vampire’ (1994), and ‘Legends of the Fall’ (1994). He later earned his first Oscar nomination for ‘12 Monkeys’ (1995). What solidified his career was his feature in ‘Fight Club’ (1999), along with Steven Soderbergh's ‘Ocean's Eleven’ (2001) franchise.Brad Pitt’s stint as a producerBeyond acting, the star also dabbled in producing films and gained critical acclaim for his work in ‘Moneyball’ (2011), and later won his first Academy Award for Best Picture as a producer on ‘12 Years a Slave’ (2013), which was followed by an Oscar for Best Supporting Actor in ‘Once Upon a Time in Hollywood’ (2019).About Brad Pitt’s personal lifeOn the personal front, Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie’s relationship was heavily publicized, from the moment they started dating to their separation and their ongoing legal battle over their jointly owned vineyard. He was also once engaged to Gwyneth Paltrow and was briefly married to Jennifer Aniston from 2000 to 2005.He married Jolie in 2014 after years of staying together for years before that. The couple filed for divorce in 2016, and their settlement was finalized on December 30, 2024, ending an eight-year legal battle. As for their family, Pitt shares six children with Angelina Jolie: Maddox, Pax, Zahara, Shiloh, Knox, and Vivienne; however, he is estranged from all of his children after the two filed for divorce. Five of his children have also dropped his surname from their legal names and now only go by their mother’s last name.Brad Pitt is currently in a relationship with jewelry executive Ines de Ramon. The pair have been linked since late 2022, marking over three and a half years together. The two are quite serious since they live together in Los Angeles, though they have chosen to keep a relatively low-drama, grounded profile throughout their relationship. Despite all of this, the two often accompany one another to public events to show their support for their significant other. Many reports have also shared that while the couple is going strong, they have not thought about marriage or anything related to that for now.On the work front, his latest film, ‘Heart of the Beast,' was recently released in theaters worldwide.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body:
Queen Camilla is mourning the deaths of her doctor, Hannah Cain, and author Lord Jeffrey Archer, with Dr. Cain being found dead at her home and her husband, Mark Cain, arrested and charged with her murder.

Lord Jeffrey Archer passed away suddenly and peacefully at his home, with Queen Camilla praising his rich and colorful life in a statement.

King Charles was reportedly left worried and in agony after failing to connect with his longtime friend Sir Ranulph Fiennes, who has withdrawn from the spotlight due to a Parkinson's disease diagnosis.

Queen Camilla is mourning many losses, including the deaths of her doctor, Hannah Cain, and author Lord Jeffrey Archer.

According to Page Six , Dr. Cain was killed while throwing a sleepover for her three children and their friends on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. The outlet reported that she was found dead at her home and appeared to have suffered "blunt force injury to the right side of her head." Dr. Cain also reportedly sustained an injury "that could be suggestive of compression of the neck."

On October 7, prosecutors confirmed that Dr. Cain's husband, Mark Cain, has been arrested and charged with her murder. Authorities have not yet identified a motive, and Detective Insp Alix Wright confirmed that police are "in the very early stages of this investigation, working to establish the exact circumstances surrounding the woman's death."

Still, Wright urged people to come forward if they believe that "they may have information that could help our investigation."

Sources told The Sun that Camilla and King Charles have been informed of Dr. Cain's death, but they have yet to release a statement about the tragedy.

Camilla is also grieving the death of Lord Jeffrey Archer, a former politician and bestselling author who died "suddenly and peacefully at his home" on Monday, October 5. He was 86.

In a statement per Hello! , the Queen said, "Seldom does an author get to live a life as rich, varied and colourful as any of the characters in their books, or with as many surprising plot twists."

"While he was not without flaw, his friends will recall him as an irrepressible life force through all the many differing chapters of his life," the statement continued. "Wherever the next page turns to, I trust there will be champagne and shepherd's pie in abundance."

Camilla's recent heartbreak comes amid many reports claiming Charles was in "agony" after a devastating health update. According to RadarOnline , the King was left worried after failing to connect with his longtime friend Sir Ranulph Fiennes, an explorer who's withdrawn from the spotlight amid his Parkinson's disease diagnosis.

"The King cares enormously about Ran and was genuinely troubled and in a bit of agony when he heard what was happening," an insider explained. "This isn't somebody he knows casually – there is a friendship stretching back decades. It's especially distressing with Charles fighting cancer. He has developed the feeling that he wants no one in pain."

The source noted that Charles' "instinct was simply to reach out privately, express his concern and ask whether there was anything he could do." However, not being able to "establish contact has been incredibly upsetting."

"For somebody of the King's position to make a personal effort like that and then find the door effectively closed was difficult," they added. "His concern has always been for his friend's welfare."

Anton Bowring, also an explorer, reportedly reached out to Buckingham Palace sometime in 2025 and revealed that Fiennes was "in a very poor state." Charles' then-equerry, William Thornton, allegedly told Bowring that the King "was most concerned" and wanted to write to Fiennes and his family to offer help. However, Fiennes' wife, Louise Millington-Cotes, turned down the request because she "apparently had issues with their personal information being shared."

articles.title: Breaking Bad star Aaron Paul ditches LA for life in France, sells $7.495 million home after a year on market; 4,026-square-foot Seyler House was listed at $10 million in July 2025
articles.summary: Breaking Bad star Aaron Paul has sold his Los Angeles home, known as the Seyler House, for $7.495 million after the luxury property spent more than a year
articles.body: Breaking Bad star Aaron Paul has sold his Los Angeles home, known as the Seyler House, for $7.495 million after the luxury property spent more than a year on the market. The Aaron Paul Los Angeles home was originally listed for around $10 million in July 2025 before the actor reduced the asking price.The 47-year-old actor, best known for playing Jesse Pinkman in the hit series Breaking Bad, has sold his three-bedroom, three-and-a-half-bathroom home near Griffith Park, according to a report by TMZ.The Aaron Paul house was initially put on the market in July 2025 with an asking price of approximately $10 million. After failing to sell for more than a year, the Los Angeles property saw its price reduced to $8.2 million in January.Paul ultimately accepted $7.495 million for the residence.Inside Aaron Paul's Seyler House in Los FelizThe property, known as the Seyler House, is located in the Los Feliz neighbourhood of Los Angeles. Built in 1922, the 4,026-square-foot residence sits behind gates on nearly 1.5 acres of land.The historic Los Angeles home was originally designed by renowned architect Stiles O. Clements, while its interiors were later renovated by Commune Design.The property features beams and high ceilings that open onto patios and terraces. Its amenities include a media room, card room and guest bedroom.The kitchen connects directly to an outdoor patio with a dining area overlooking the garden. The primary suite includes a bathroom, a large dressing area and a private balcony.Aaron Paul home features pool, koi pond and Los Angeles viewsThe outdoor spaces are among the highlights of the Aaron Paul Los Angeles house. The gated estate features a swimming pool, cold plunge, fireplace, fire pit and koi pond.The property also offers panoramic views of Los Angeles, adding to its appeal as a luxury celebrity residence.Paul is not the only famous name associated with the Seyler House. Previous residents of the property reportedly include actors Robert Pattinson, Noah Wyle and Jim Parsons, basketball legend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and the late actor Tim Curry.Why Aaron Paul moved from Los Angeles to ParisPaul's decision to sell his Los Angeles home comes after he and his family relocated to Paris following the January 2025 wildfires in the Los Angeles area.Speaking to the Daily Mail in November last year, the Breaking Bad actor explained that the fires prompted the family to reconsider their life in Los Angeles."When the fires happened in LA, we just knew that we were done with LA, so we sold our house in LA and moved to Paris," Paul said. "Paris is awesome."The actor said he and his wife, Lauren Parsekian, had always dreamed of spending a year abroad and decided to make the move for their children."We just always wanted to be around a completely different culture," Paul added.Aaron Paul said the home was a 'safe haven' for his familyDespite selling the property, Paul has spoken warmly about his years at the Los Angeles residence.According to People, the actor previously described the home as a "safe haven" for his family and said they felt fortunate to have experienced so much life there."We will forever hold this home and its history close to our hearts," Paul said.Paul shares two children with wife Lauren Parsekian - eight-year-old daughter Story Annabelle and four-year-old son Ryden Caspian.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Mel Gibson: 'Nothing ever goes according to plan. But the mistake is to think that the journey was not worth it,' a powerful life lesson on accepting what we cannot control and moving forward
articles.summary: Explore Mel Gibson's powerful quote on accepting life's uncertainties and the importance of learning from our experiences. Discover how his journey reflects the reality of navigating unexpected challenges.
articles.body: You can’t have 'Mad Max' or 'Lethal Weapon' without Mel Gibson. His portrayal of Martin Riggs, the loose-cannon cop with a death wish, and Max Rockatansky, the road warrior haunted by loss, made him one of the biggest movie stars of the 1980s and 90s. But what makes his story worth examining isn't just the box office numbers.It's what he said when asked about doubt. Gibson was asked if he had ever seriously doubted his faith. His answer wasn't about religion. It was about life. He said, "You have to be prepared to accept that most of life is out of your hands," in a 2002 interview with The Independent. His statement from that same interaction provides today's quote of the day.Motivational quote of the day by Mel Gibson reads: "Nothing ever goes according to plan, but the mistake is to think that the journey was not worth it.”What does the quote by Mel Gibson really mean?Life doesn't follow the script you write for it. Plans fail. Careers take detours. Relationships end. Projects fall apart. The practical meaning is this: when a plan falls apart, you have a choice. You can either decide the whole thing was a waste, or you can look at what actually happened and ask what it taught you. A failed project can teach you patience. A rejection can redirect your career. A difficult period can force you to understand yourself more honestly than success ever would. None of that makes the pain good. But it can make the experience worth something even if the destination wasn't what you wanted. His point is that judging the entire journey by whether it matched the original plan is a mistake. It's also, in his words, "a lack of humility".He further adds, "You have to be prepared to accept that most of life is out of your hands". Gibson has lived through public scandals, industry blacklisting, and personal turmoil that he has spoken about openly.How is the quote by Mel Gibson still relevant today?People are more obsessed with control than ever. Careers are mapped out. Goals are measured in five-year increments. Every setback is treated as a failure of planning rather than a normal part of being alive. Gibson's quote pushes back on that. It says the detours are where the real life happens. The failed project that taught you something. The rejection that sent you in a different direction. The plan that fell apart and forced you to figure out what you actually wanted.His words also speak to anyone dealing with a setback they didn't see coming. A layoff. A health scare. A relationship ending. The instinct is to look back and decide the whole thing was a waste. Gibson is saying that's the wrong question. The question is what you learned, what you became, and whether you kept going. He did. That's the lesson.Early life of Mel GibsonMel Columcille Gerard Gibson was born on January 3, 1956, in Peekskill, New York. He was the sixth of eleven children. He’s the 6th child of Anne Reilly and Hutton Gibson; his father was a railroad brakeman. The family moved to Australia when Gibson was twelve years old. During his high school years, Gibson was educated by members of the Congregation of Christian Brothers at St Leo's Catholic College in Wahroonga, New South Wales.He studied acting at the National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA) in Sydney. His screen debut came in 1976 with 'Summer City', while he was still a student. He graduated in 1977. A year later, he auditioned for a low-budget Australian film called 'Mad Max'. He was one of over 200 actors who tried out. He showed up with a bruised face from a bar fight the night before. The directors thought the damage made him look dangerous. He got the part.Mel Gibson's rise to fame'Mad Max' (1979) became a global hit and one of the most profitable films ever made relative to its budget. His follow-up film, Mad Max 2: The Road Warrior (1981), secured his status as an international star. He also starred in Peter Weir's Gallipoli (1981) around the same time, receiving critical praise.In 1987, he starred in 'Lethal Weapon' as Martin Riggs. The buddy-cop film became a massive franchise, spawning three sequels. By the early 1990s, Gibson was one of the highest-paid actors in Hollywood. He starred in 'Hamlet' (1990), 'The Patriot' (2000), and 'What Women Want' (2000).Then he stepped behind the camera. In 1995, he directed and starred in 'Braveheart', the story of Scottish warrior William Wallace. The film won five Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director for Gibson. It was his first time directing a feature film. He followed it with the co-writing and directing of 'The Passion of the Christ' (2004). The film was a huge commercial success, grossing over $600 million worldwide on a $30 million budget.His career has been marked by both triumph and controversy. He has faced public scandals that led to a period of professional exile. But he kept working. He directed 'Hacksaw Ridge' in 2016, which earned him another Academy Award nomination for Best Director. He is currently preparing 'The Resurrection of the Christ', a two-part sequel to 'The Passion of the Christ'. articles.summary: Bryan Seaver's expletive-filled emails about Nashville hotel security surfaced in court documents filed just days before Dolly Parton's death.
articles.body: Dolly Parton’s nephew unleashed an expletive-filled tirade in an email exchange involving the country music legend just days before her death as tensions over security services boiled over, according to court documents obtained by Fox News Digital. Bryan Seaver, Parton's nephew and longtime head of security, fired off the profanity-laced message Aug. 21, four days before Parton's death, in an email chain carrying the subject line "Fwd: Letter from Dolly." "Hi Billy. Message received," Seaver began. "If you think my harsh language is too much for your failing vendors to digest, just wait until my lawyers start f---ing you up the a--." DOLLY PARTON’S SISTERS PUSH BACK ON FEUD RUMORS AFTER NEPHEW’S LEGAL BATTLE WITH STAR'S ESTATE ERUPTS While it's unclear who Billy is, Parton’s longtime manager, Danny Nozell, and other members of her team were included in the email chain. "I challenge you to bring spurious and feeble complaints. Let’s play ball you f---ing s---bag loser," he continued. Seaver also blasted the progress of an apparent Nashville project, alleging the build-out was "late and worrisome" and subcontractors "continue to do drugs in our venue." "Explain to your shareholders why your project is still failing and your building is unfinished, unoccupied and mired in violations," he wrote. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? "Tell Mr. [redacted] to call me and we’ll talk man to man. Otherwise, your doom ensues." The court exhibit does not reveal the contents of the apparent "Letter from Dolly" referenced in the subject line. DOLLY PARTON’S SISTER REVEALS ‘LAST THING’ COUNTRY LEGEND ASKED OF HER BEFORE DEATH The email came just two days after Seaver directly invoked his famous aunt while complaining about security arrangements at a Nashville hotel project. "Your contract security company (Titan) you’ve hired in spite of me and Dolly’s request for service at the hotel has completely f---ed up and let an employee be assaulted," Seaver alleged in the Aug. 19 email. "Let me know when you are ready to hand the security situation completely over to Dolly’s contracted service providers in Nashville and I will fix your problem," he added. "SAPS (Seaver’s Squadron Augmented Protection Services) is your answer." The combative exchanges marked a dramatic shift from correspondence less than three months earlier. On May 29, Seaver offered to help staff and train security personnel in Nashville. The recipient, identified as "Bill," thanked him for his "genuine care and concern" and said he hoped both teams would support "each other in success." Parton died Aug. 25 at age 80 after a brief battle with cancer. Seaver, who had served as Parton's head of security for more than two decades, was chosen by his aunt to publicly announce her death. Less than a month later, tensions between Seaver and members of Parton's business circle spilled into court. As Fox News Digital previously reported, Parton's manager, Nozell, who runs She’s Alive, LLC, sought a restraining order against Seaver and his company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services. She's Alive is an entity Parton created to oversee her business interests. DOLLY PARTON LAID TO REST AS NIECE SHARES EMOTIONAL TRIBUTE TO ‘GRANNY’ A Tennessee judge granted a temporary restraining order, citing an alleged pattern of threats and demands for payment, along with Seaver's "claimed access to weapons, experience with violence, and intention to retaliate." The order barred Seaver and his company from entering She’s Alive properties, coming within 1,000 feet of its employees and business partners or contacting them. She’s Alive alleged Seaver's communications continued to escalate after Parton's death. In a Sept. 1 message included in earlier court filings, Seaver allegedly threatened to start a podcast aimed at damaging Parton's business relationships unless he was paid. According to documents previously obtained by Fox News Digital, the alleged messages prompted several employees to resign, Parton's trust and estate attorney to step away and She’s Alive to hire private security to protect employees at work and at home. Seaver was fired Sept. 15 over what the company characterized as "terrorizing conduct." articles.title: Paramore's Hayley Williams targets Christian nationalism as America's 'greatest threat' to democracy
articles.summary: Hayley Williams called Christian nationalism the greatest threat to American democracy at a recent concert, drawing sharp pushback.
articles.body: Paramore frontwoman Hayley Williams faced criticism after telling fans during a September concert that Christian nationalism is "the greatest threat to American democracy," adding another political declaration to a tour where she had repeatedly spoken out against President Donald Trump, immigration enforcement and Israel's war in Gaza. In the recirculated clip, Williams made the declaration before performing "True Believer," a track from her 2025 solo album, "Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party." Her statement specifically targeted Christian nationalism, rather than Christians or Christianity broadly. "The greatest threat to American democracy is Christian nationalism," Williams said. ED SHEERAN CONCERTGOERS WARN ARTISTS ABOUT SHARING POLITICAL VIEWS: 'YOU'RE GOING TO ALIENATE' FANS Lisa Cusack, president of the Don’t L.A. My Burbank PAC, told Fox News Digital that Williams’ comment ignored Christianity’s influence on the nation’s founding principles and democratic system. "Incredibly ignorant comment considering Christianity is woven into the fabric of every founding document that proscribes Americans' democratic rights," she said. "There would be no Natural Law without Christianity, and without that, no human rights that exist beyond a government’s power. Christianity sees all people as made in the image of God, so are all valuable, no matter how successful, and puts self-sacrifice above power." "Democracy has thrived in the Christian nations across the world for a reason. The true threat is this kind of ignorant bigotry," she continued. At another recent concert, Williams also recently shouted "F--- ICE" and "FREE MOTHERF------ PALESTINE!" while performing her song, "Ice in My OJ," prompting a response from the Department of Homeland Security. SPRINGSTEEN, OTHER STARS SHARE STAGE WITH HARDCORE LEFTIST GROUPS AT MUSIC FEST A DHS spokesperson responded to Williams’ anti-ICE remarks by defending federal immigration officers and urging the singer to recognize their work. "America is grateful all the time for our federal law enforcement officers who keep us safe," the spokesperson said, in a statement to Fox News Digital. "We suggest Ms. Williams to thank them for their service, not belittle their sacrifice." Williams has incorporated political commentary into her performances for years. During Paramore's performance at the 2024 iHeartRadio Music Festival, the singer warned concertgoers against returning Trump to the White House and accused him of supporting an agenda that would harm women, poor Americans, racial minorities and the LGBTQ community. Williams framed that presidential election as a decision about the future of American democracy. SINGER PHIL COLLINS BLASTS TRUMP AS 'NASTY,' TEASES SONG ABOUT AMERICA CALLED 'FAT PEOPLE WITH GUNS' "Project 2025 is Donald Trump’s playbook for controlling and punishing women, poor people, people of color, and the LGBTQ+ community," she said. "It is time for all Americans to band together and to finally defeat the Trump agenda. And the only way to do that is by confronting him at the polls. "Do you want to live in a dictatorship? Well, show up and vote," she continued. After saying she was comfortable discussing politics, Williams singled out supporters of then-presidential candidate Ron DeSantis. "If you vote for Ron DeSantis, you’re f------ dead to me," Williams said. articles.body: Sebastian Maniscalco has found himself in hot water with some comedians who are claiming that his new SiriusXM channel is taking away money and exposure from working-class comics. articles.title: Tom Cruise’s ‘Digger’ Will Lose $250 Million | Exclusive
articles.summary: Tom Cruise's climate change comedy Digger will lose $250 million after a disastrous opening weekend box office of just $8 million.
articles.body:
"Digger," the quirky, end-of-the-world satire starring Tom Cruise, is poised to lose a stunning $250 million by the end of its run, TheWrap has learned, even when factoring in post-theatrical revenue. It is by far the biggest loss for the movie star, and one of the largest losses in recent years of movie releases.

Skydance executives were shocked to learn the extent of the loss of the Warner Bros. movie directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu when the company was handed over this week.

Previous reports put the projected loss at approximately $125 million, but it is expected to be more extensive after earning just $8 million domestically and $21 million globally at the box office in its opening weekend.

The film is not expected to exceed $40 million in worldwide box office, according to insiders at Skydance.

A Warner Bros. representative had no comment.

The budget of the movie, according to multiple insiders, was $173 million, though part of that was due to an unexpected insurance settlement. Another insider put the final budget at $163 million. The marketing budget was about $100 million, mostly related to Cruise's global press tour.

The film was also fully financed by Warner Bros., unlike other projects like "Dune," which often have financial partners.

The film, with Cruise playing a a rich oil magnate whose wells trigger a global environmental catastrophe, garnered mixed reviews, with some finding the film confusing while others hailed it as bold and comically over the top.

Cruise, the world's biggest movie star, is barely recognizable as Digger, a paunchy, balding billionaire living with a dying cat among mounted stuffed animals.

"Digger" was one of several big swings on auteur filmmakers from Warner Bros. Pictures heads Pam Abdy and Mike De Luca. Some worked, like "Sinners" ($327 million, 4 Oscars) and "One Battle After Another" ($213 million, 6 Oscars, including Best Picture). Others, like Maggie Gyllenhaal's "The Bride!" ($24 million), did not.

But "Digger" was considered a coup when first greenlit (by David Zaslav himself, TheWrap is told), as it marked the first film in a new pact with Cruise — one of the biggest movie stars in the world — to make original and franchise films with Warner Bros. Pairing him with Iñárritu, one of only three directors to win back-to-back Best Director Oscars, seemed like a no-brainer. But after a decade and a half of entertaining audiences by showing he could do really-for-real death-defying stunts, Cruise's appeal didn't carry over to a heavy-prosthetic transformation in a climate change satire.

De Luca and Abdy were dismissed by David Ellison, who has put Paramount's Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein in charge of overseeing the film output for both Paramount and Warner Bros. under the newly formed Skydance.

They'll have another stab at a Tom Cruise hit in "Days of Thunder 2," which starts production next year for Paramount and co-stars Anne Hathaway.

articles.title: Dafydd Owain wins Welsh Music Prize 2026 for second album
articles.summary: A total of 15 albums were shortlisted for the £10,000 top prize across a range of genres.
articles.body:
Singer Dafydd Owain has won the 2026 Welsh Music Prize with his album Ymarfer Byw.

A total of 15 albums were shortlisted for the £10,000 top prize across genres from rap and metal to pop, folk, rock and indie rock.

Receiving his award at Wales Millennium Centre in Cardiff on Wednesday, Owain, from Caernarfon, said the last time he had performed on the same stage was as a 16-year-old choir member.

"I mimed the whole thing because I was... scared of making a bum note," he recalled.

"It's weird to have an award for what's essentially singing now," he told the audience.

Owain acknowledged "one big family" of people, including his band members, who he said contributed to his success.

In August, he won the Welsh Language Album of the Year award with his second album.

Singer Mary Hopkin, from Pontardawe, Swansea, who was one of the first artists signed to The Beatles' label Apple Records, received the Welsh Music Inspiration Award for her contribution to music over several decades.

Her daughter, Jessica Lee Morgan, spoke to BBC Radio Wales - which broadcast the awards live on Wednesday - and said her mother was "very honoured" to receive the recognition.

She accepted the award on her mother's behalf and performed a medley of her hits.

Gwenifer Raymond - Last Night I Heard the Dog Star Bark

The awards, hosted by BBC Radio 1 DJ and presenter Sian Eleri, included live performances from some of the nominees.

The competition also honoured emerging talent with this year's Triskel Award winners named as singer Betsan, and bands Casual Smart and MWSOG.

Last year Don Leisure won the Welsh Music Prize for his album Tyrchu Sain, which honours the legacy of Welsh music while reframing it for a new generation.

The album saw the Cardiff-based producer, whose real name is Aly Jamal, dig through the archives of Sain Records to create new music from forgotten recordings. The word "trychu" translates as digging.

It features appearances including previous Welsh Music Prize winners Gruff Rhys and Boy Azooga's Dave Newington.

articles.title: Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs ordered by court to pay $477,700 after losing $100 million defamation lawsuit against NBCUniversal documentary as nearly $1 million fee demand was reduced
articles.summary: Sean “Diddy” Combs has been ordered to pay $477,700.50 in attorneys’ fees to NBCUniversal, Peacock TV and production company Ample after losing his $100
articles.body: Sean “Diddy” Combs has been ordered to pay $477,700.50 in attorneys’ fees to NBCUniversal, Peacock TV and production company Ample after losing his $100 million defamation lawsuit over the documentary Diddy: The Making of a Bad Boy. A New York judge substantially reduced the nearly $1 million fee request, finding portions of the defendants’ legal bills excessive and unreasonable.Justice Phaedra F. Perry-Bond of the New York Supreme Court issued the decision on October 6, awarding the defendants $477,700.50.NBCUniversal and the other defendants had asked for $990,292 in attorneys’ fees after successfully defending against Combs’ lawsuit. The court ultimately cut the request by $512,591.50, awarding less than half of the amount sought.The judge did not reduce the lawyers’ hourly rates but found that some of the hours billed were excessive.The court particularly reduced fees connected with internal meetings, preparation for oral arguments and work on the defendants’ reply to Combs’ opposition to the fee request. According to the court record, the defendants had billed 777.5 hours through six attorneys, plus another 54.3 hours for responding to Combs’ opposition.Combs’ spokesperson Juda Engelmayer pointed to the reduction in the requested amount.“NBCUniversal sought nearly $1 million in attorneys’ fees, and the Court found substantial portions of those fees excessive and unreasonable,” Engelmayer said in a statement to PEOPLE, noting that the court reduced the request by more than $512,000.Combs had sued NBCUniversal for $100 millionThe legal-fee ruling stems from a lawsuit Combs filed in New York in February 2025 over Peacock's documentary Diddy: The Making of a Bad Boy.Combs sued NBCUniversal Media, Peacock TV and Ample Entertainment, alleging that the documentary contained defamatory claims and caused serious damage to his reputation. He sought at least $100 million in damages.Among his allegations, Combs claimed the documentary “shamelessly advances conspiracy theories” and repeatedly insinuated that he was a serial killer.The documentary included interviews with people who accused Combs of sexual misconduct as well as former associates. Singer Al B. Sure! appeared in the film and discussed the death of Combs’ former partner Kim Porter, contributing to speculation addressed in the documentary.Court dismissed Combs’ lawsuit in AprilCombs' amended complaint was dismissed by Justice Perry-Bond in April 2026.The court determined that the lawsuit constituted a strategic lawsuit against public participation, or SLAPP, under New York's anti-SLAPP law. Because the defendants prevailed on their motion under the applicable provisions of New York Civil Rights Law, they became eligible for attorneys’ fees.The judge later considered the defendants’ application for reimbursement of their legal expenses.In the October 6 ruling, the court concluded that the defendants were entitled to fees but rejected substantial portions of the amount they had requested.Among the reductions, the judge found that nearly $100,000 billed for internal meetings, discussions and calls was excessive and reduced that portion by 80%. The court also substantially reduced fees associated with preparation for oral arguments.Judge says documentary did not create the alleged reputational damageThe fee decision follows the court's earlier rejection of Combs’ defamation claims.In that ruling, the judge questioned how the documentary could have created additional reputational damage given the extensive negative publicity and legal allegations surrounding Combs before the film's release.The documentary was released amid extensive public scrutiny of Combs, including civil lawsuits and his federal criminal case.Combs' lawsuit argued that NBCUniversal and the documentary's producers used false allegations to profit from his name and reputation. The defendants disputed his claims.Combs remains in federal prisonCombs is currently serving a 50-month federal prison sentence at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey.A federal jury found him guilty in 2025 on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution. He was acquitted of the more serious charges of sex trafficking and racketeering conspiracy.His conviction and sentence remain subject to appeal.His projected release date has changed several times during his incarceration. Bureau of Prisons records had listed January 21, 2028, in late September, but a PEOPLE report published October 8 said the projected date had subsequently moved to March 2, 2028. articles.body: Angelina Jolie's lawyer has criticised Brad Pitt's latest legal attempt to obtain her financial records, calling it another effort to control the narrative surrounding their long-running dispute over Chateau Miraval.Judge rejects Brad Pitt's request for Angelina Jolie's financial recordsThis comes after a judge rejected Pitt's request for Jolie to hand over her financial records from 2017 to 2019. The records were sought as part of the ongoing legal battle over their French winery. According to the ruling, the court found that Pitt's side had 'not demonstrated sufficient cause' to override Jolie's privacy interests.However, the judge left the door open for Pitt to renew his request if Jolie's testimony ultimately puts her income from those years at issue.Brad Pitt of trying to control the narrative?Following the ruling, Jolie's attorney Paul Murphy criticised the request and told TMZ, "This is a motion Brad never should've brought."He further alleged, "Mr. Pitt's unyielding demand for harassing information is just the latest manifestation of his attempts to control her and the narratives in this case. What Angelina wants and has always wanted is to untangle her personal and financial life from her ex-husband. Rather than do the right thing and buy her out at an agreed price, Mr. Pitt at the last minute tried to use her exit from Miraval as leverage to force her [to] sign an NDA to cover up his abuse of her and their children.
